info.title: Cloudflare Email Security
info.description: Cloudflare Email Security: email routing rules, addresses, and email security settings.

get.description: Returns an aggregated monthly email security report including detections, dispositions, and policy activity for the trailing 12 months.

200.description: Monthly report for the trailing 12 months.

by_month.description: A map of month (YYYY-MM) to the disposition counts recorded for that month.

get.description: Returns information for each email that matches the provided search parameters.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The beginning of the search date range. Defaults to `now - 30 days`. Must not be in the future.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the search date range. Defaults to `now`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Space-delimited term matched case-insensitively against message metadata — sender, recipient, subject, attachment names and hashes, and message ID.

parameters.name: detections_only
parameters.description: Whether to include only detections in search results.

parameters.name: final_disposition
parameters.description: Dispositions to filter by.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Metric to aggregate the results by.

parameters.name: message_action
parameters.description: Message actions to filter by.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Filter by recipient. Matches an email address or a domain.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Filter by sender. Matches an email address or a domain.

parameters.name: smtp_helo_ip
parameters.description: Matches messages whose SMTP HELO server IP address equals this value.

parameters.name: alert_id
parameters.description: Filter by alert ID.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Filter by a domain found in the email — sender domain, recipient domain, or a domain in a link.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: Filter by the RFC 5322 Message-ID header.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Search for messages containing individual keywords in any order within the subject.

parameters.name: delivery_status
parameters.description: Delivery status to filter by.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response's `result_info`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Deprecated: Use cursor pagination instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.

200.description: Search results for the provided query.

202.description: The search is taking longer than expected. Use the Location header to poll for results.

Location.description: URL to poll for search results.

result.description: Always empty on 202; follow the Location header to retrieve results.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of bulk action jobs for the account.

parameters.name: action_type
parameters.description: Filter jobs by the action they perform.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter jobs by their processing status.

post.description: Creates a new bulk action job to move or release messages that match the provided search parameters. To move or release an explicit list of known messages instead of a search, use the move or release endpoints.

delete.description: Deletes the job, removing it from all list and detail endpoints. Only jobs in a terminal state (`COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, or `FAILED`) can be deleted. To stop an in-progress job without removing it, use the cancel endpoint instead.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation permanently deletes the completed, cancelled, or failed bulk action job from all list and detail endpoints.

get.description: Returns the status and details of a specific bulk action job.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the bulk action job.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the bulk action job to cancel.

post.description: Cancels the job, marking it as cancelled and stopping any pending message processing. The job record remains visible in list and detail endpoints.

get.summary: List messages for a bulk action job
get.description: Returns the individual messages associated with a bulk action job, including their processing status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter the job's messages by their processing status.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the bulk action job whose messages to list.

post.description: Moves one or more messages to a specified mailbox folder (Inbox, JunkEmail, DeletedItems, RecoverableItemsDeletions, or RecoverableItemsPurges). Requires active integration. Operates on an explicit list of messages; to move all messages matching a search, create a bulk action job instead.

expected_disposition.description: Nonfunctional field. End of life: December 1, 2026.

ids.description: List of message IDs to move.

postfix_ids.description: Deprecated, use `ids` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.

post.summary: Generate preview for a non-detection message
post.description: Generates a preview image for a message that was not flagged as a detection. The message is rendered from the copy in the recipient's mailbox, so this requires an active integration and only works while the message is still in the recipient's inbox. Returns a base64-encoded PNG screenshot of the email body. For messages with a detection, use the detection preview endpoint instead.

Delivers one or more quarantined messages to their intended recipients, for cases where a message was incorrectly quarantined. Operates on an explicit list of messages; to release all messages matching a search, create a bulk action job instead. The response includes delivery status for each recipient.

requestBody.description: The messages to release, identified by their investigate IDs.

ids.description: Investigate IDs of the messages to release.

get.description: Retrieves comprehensive details for a specific email message including headers, recipients, sender information, and current quarantine status. Use the investigate_id from search results to fetch detailed information.

get.summary: List post-delivery actions for a message
get.description: Returns the list of post-delivery actions (moves, quarantine releases, previews, etc.) that have been applied to a specific email message.
Returns detection details such as threat categories and sender information for messages with a detection.

post.description: Moves a single message to a specified mailbox folder (Inbox, JunkEmail, DeletedItems, RecoverableItemsDeletions, or RecoverableItemsPurges). Requires active integration.

expected_disposition.description: Nonfunctional field. End of life: December 1, 2026.

get.description: Returns a preview of the message body as a base64-encoded PNG image for any message with a detection. For messages without a detection, use the non-detection preview endpoint instead.
Returns the raw EML content of any message with a detection.

post.description: Submits a request to reclassify an email's disposition. Use for reporting false positives or false negatives. Optionally provide the raw EML content for reanalysis. The reclassification is processed asynchronously. Deprecated; use the create submissions endpoint instead.

get.description: Retrieves delivery and processing trace information for an email message. Shows the delivery path, retraction history, and move operations performed on the message. Useful for debugging delivery issues.
Retrieves PhishGuard security alert reports for a specified date range. Reports include detected threats, dispositions, and contextual information. Use for security monitoring and threat analysis.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the time range (RFC3339). Takes precedence over from_date.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End of the time range (RFC3339). Takes precedence over to_date.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Deprecated, use `start` instead. Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: Deprecated, use `end` instead. End date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of email allow policies. These policies exempt matching emails from security detection, allowing them to bypass disposition actions. Supports filtering by pattern type and policy attributes.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

parameters.name: is_exempt_recipient
parameters.description: Filter to show only policies where messages to the recipient bypass all detections.

parameters.name: is_trusted_sender
parameters.description: Filter to show only policies where messages from the sender bypass all detections and link following.

parameters.name: is_acceptable_sender
parameters.description: Filter to show only policies where messages from the sender are exempted from Spam, Spoof, and Bulk dispositions (not Malicious or Suspicious).

parameters.name: verify_sender
parameters.description: Filter to show only policies that enforce DMARC, SPF, or DKIM authentication.

parameters.name: pattern_type
parameters.description: Filter by pattern type.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Filter by exact pattern value.

post.description: Creates a new allow policy that exempts matching emails from security detections. Use with caution as this bypasses email security scanning. Policies can match on sender patterns and apply to specific detections or all detections.

Executes multiple allow policy operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create allow policies in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the allow policies to delete.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the policy's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the policy's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may delete the selected allow policies and restore normal security scanning and disposition actions for matching emails.

delete.description: Removes an allow policy. After deletion, emails matching this pattern will be subject to normal security scanning and disposition actions.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the allow policy and restores normal security scanning and disposition actions for matching emails.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific allow policy including its pattern, dispositions that are exempted, and whether it applies to all detections.

patch.description: Updates an existing allow policy. Only provided fields will be modified. Changes take effect for new emails matching the pattern.

put.description: Replaces an existing allow policy in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing policies declaratively.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of blocked email sender patterns. These patterns prevent emails from matching senders from being delivered. Supports filtering by pattern type and searching across patterns.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

parameters.name: pattern_type
parameters.description: Filter by pattern type.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Filter by pattern value.

post.description: Creates a new blocked sender pattern. Emails matching this pattern will be blocked from delivery. Patterns can be email addresses, domains, or IP addresses, and support regular expressions.

Executes multiple blocked sender operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create blocked sender patterns in a single request. All four operation
arrays (deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the blocked sender patterns to delete.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may delete the selected blocked sender patterns and stop automatically blocking matching emails based on those rules.

delete.description: Removes a blocked sender pattern. After deletion, emails from this sender will no longer be automatically blocked based on this rule.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the blocked sender pattern and stops automatically blocking matching emails based on this rule.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific blocked sender pattern including its pattern type, value, and metadata.

patch.description: Updates an existing blocked sender pattern. Only provided fields will be modified. The pattern will continue blocking emails until deleted.

put.description: Replaces an existing blocked sender pattern in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing blocked senders declaratively.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of content policies. These policies match against the subject or body of emails using a pattern. Supports filtering by name or enabled status, and searching across name and pattern fields.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Filter by enabled status.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter by exact policy name.

post.description: Creates a new content policy. Emails whose subject or body matches the pattern will be subject to the configured action.

Executes multiple content policy operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create content policies in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the content policies to delete.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the policy's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the policy's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may delete the selected content policies and stop evaluating emails against their patterns.

delete.description: Removes a content policy. After deletion, emails will no longer be evaluated against this pattern.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the content policy and stops evaluating emails against its pattern.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific content policy including its pattern, targets, and metadata.

patch.description: Updates an existing content policy. Only provided fields will be modified.

delete.description: Removes protection from multiple email domains. Deprecated; use the batch endpoint instead.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation permanently deletes protection for the selected email domains. Emails for these domains will no longer be processed by Email Security.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of email domains protected by Email Security. Includes domain configuration, delivery modes, and authorization status. Supports filtering by delivery mode and integration ID.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

parameters.name: allowed_delivery_mode
parameters.description: Delivery mode to filter by.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain names to filter by.

parameters.name: active_delivery_mode
parameters.description: Currently active delivery mode to filter by.

parameters.name: integration_id
parameters.description: Integration ID to filter by.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filters response to domains with the provided status.

post.description: Protects a new email domain by adding it to Email Security. Accepts a flat configuration object covering all delivery modes. Returns the newly created domain configuration.

Executes multiple domain operations in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the domains to remove protection from.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the domain's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the domain's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may permanently delete protection for the selected email domains. Emails for those domains will no longer be processed by Email Security.

delete.description: Removes email security protection from a domain. After deletion, emails for this domain will no longer be processed by Email Security. This action cannot be undone.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation permanently deletes protection for the email domain. Emails for this domain will no longer be processed by Email Security.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific protected email domain including its delivery configuration, SPF/DMARC status, and authorization state.

patch.description: Updates configuration for a protected email domain. Only provided fields will be modified. Changes affect delivery mode, security settings, and regional processing.

put.description: Replaces all mutable fields of a protected email domain in a single atomic operation. Unlike PATCH, all non-computed fields are required.

get.description:
Returns the DNS TXT record information when the domain ownership isn't
verified through Cloudflare zone ownership or CASB integration.

Returns a paginated list of protected identities in the impersonation registry. These entries define identities and email addresses to protect from impersonation attacks. Can be manually added or automatically synced from directory integrations.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

post.description: Creates a new entry in the impersonation registry to protect against impersonation. Emails attempting to impersonate this identity will be flagged. Supports regex patterns for flexible email matching.

delete.description: Removes an entry from the impersonation registry. After deletion, this identity will no longer be protected from impersonation.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the impersonation registry entry and stops protecting the identity from impersonation.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific impersonation registry entry including the protected identity, email pattern, and synchronization source if directory-synced.

patch.description: Updates an existing impersonation registry entry. Only provided fields will be modified. Directory-synced entries can't be updated.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of sending domain restrictions. These restrictions enforce TLS requirements for emails from specific domains. Mail without TLS from restricted domains will be dropped unless the subdomain is in the exclude list. Supports sorting and searching.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

post.description: Creates a new sending domain restriction to enforce TLS requirements for a domain. Emails without TLS from this domain will be dropped unless the subdomain is in the exclude list.

Executes multiple delete operations on sending domain restrictions atomically. All operations succeed or fail together as a transaction. Currently only supports batch deletion. Removes TLS enforcement requirements for the specified domains.

deletes.description: IDs of the sending domain restrictions to delete.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the selected sending domain restrictions and removes TLS enforcement for the specified domains.

delete.description: Removes a sending domain restriction. After deletion, TLS will no longer be enforced for emails from this domain.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the sending domain restriction and removes TLS enforcement for emails from this domain.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific sending domain restriction including the domain requiring TLS and any excluded subdomains exempt from the TLS requirement.

patch.description: Updates an existing sending domain restriction. Only provided fields will be modified. Changes affect which domains require TLS and which subdomains are excluded.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of trusted domain patterns. Trusted domains prevent false positives for recently registered domains and lookalike domain detections. Patterns can use regular expressions for flexible matching.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

parameters.name: is_recent
parameters.description: Filter to show only recently registered domains that are trusted to prevent triggering Suspicious or Malicious dispositions.

parameters.name: is_similarity
parameters.description: Filter to show only proximity domains (partner or approved domains with similar spelling to connected domains) that prevent Spoof dispositions.

post.description: Creates a new trusted domain pattern. Use for partner domains or approved senders that should bypass recent domain registration and similarity checks. Configure whether it prevents recent domain or spoof dispositions.

Executes multiple trusted domain operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create trusted domain patterns in a single request. All four operation
arrays (deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the trusted domain patterns to delete.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may delete the selected trusted domain patterns and restore normal recent domain and similarity checks for matching emails.

delete.description: Removes a trusted domain pattern. After deletion, emails from this domain will be subject to normal recent domain and similarity checks.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the trusted domain pattern and restores normal recent domain and similarity checks for matching emails.

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific trusted domain pattern including its pattern value, whether it uses regex matching, and which detection types it affects.

patch.description: Updates an existing trusted domain pattern. Only provided fields will be modified. Changes take effect for new emails matching the pattern.

put.description: Replaces an existing trusted domain in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing trusted domains declaratively.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of URL rewrite ignore patterns for the account. URLs matching these patterns will not be rewritten.

200.description: List of URL ignore patterns for the provided account.

post.description: Creates a new URL rewrite ignore pattern. URLs matching this pattern will not be rewritten.

Executes multiple operations atomically. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

deletes.description: IDs of the URL ignore patterns to delete.

patches.description: Partial updates to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and only the fields to change.

puts.description: Full replacements to apply — each entry carries the pattern's ID and every field of its new value.

post.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation may delete the selected URL rewrite ignore patterns and cause matching URLs to be rewritten again.

delete.description: Removes a URL rewrite ignore pattern. After deletion, URLs matching this pattern will be rewritten again.
delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation deletes the URL rewrite ignore pattern and causes matching URLs to be rewritten again.

get.description: Returns a single URL rewrite ignore pattern by its identifier.

patch.description: Updates an existing URL rewrite ignore pattern. Only provided fields will be modified.

get.description: Returns information for submissions made to reclassify emails. Shows the status, outcome, and disposition changes for reclassification requests made by users or the security team. Useful for tracking false positive/negative reports.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The beginning of the search date range. Defaults to `now - 30 days`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the search date range. Defaults to `now`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by who created the submission — `TEAM` for security team members or `USER` for end users.

parameters.name: submission_id
parameters.description: Filter by a specific submission ID.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by review status — `escalated`, `reviewed`, or `unreviewed`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search term for filtering submissions.

parameters.name: escalated_from_user
parameters.description: When true, return only submissions that were escalated by an end user (vs. by the security team). When false, return only submissions that were not escalated by an end user. When omitted, no filter is applied.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Field to sort by.

post.description: Submits messages for reclassification or to report missed detections.

get.description: Lists destination addresses configured for Email Routing in an account.

schema.description: Maximum number of results per page.
Sorts results in an ascending or descending order.

403.description: Authentication error or missing email routing address list permission.

post.description: Create a destination address to forward your emails to. Destination addresses need to be verified before they can be used.

delete.x-forge-require-confirmation: This operation permanently deletes a destination address.

get.description: Gets information for a specific destination email already created.

patch.description: Updates the status of a specific destination address.

get.description: Lists existing routing rules across all zones in the account.

schema.description: Maximum number of results per page.

403.description: Authentication error or missing account rule list permission.

post.description: Computes the Email Routing rule changes that would be needed to reconcile a Wrangler-managed desired ruleset. This endpoint is read-only and does not create, update, or delete rules.

400.description: Error 2062: Unknown Email Routing domain. A desired address or catch-all target does not resolve to an Email Routing-enabled domain in this account.

403.description: Authentication error or missing account rule list permission.

422.description: Invalid plan input, such as malformed matchers/actions, duplicate targets, or an owner_worker_tag that does not resolve to a known Worker script.

get.description: Lists email suppressions for the specified account.

post.description: Creates a new email suppression for the specified account.

delete.description: Deletes an email suppression for the specified account.

get.description: Retrieves a single email suppression for the specified account.

Returns the current daily sending quota for the account and, when a quota is resolved, the account's current usage against it. Quota is null when not yet available; usage is null when there is no resolved quota or usage is temporarily unavailable.

403.description: Authentication error or missing email sending read permission.

get.description: Returns the raw RFC 5322 MIME message for the given account and message id.
Returns the authoritative Email Sending reputation state and active evaluation policy. Accounts without an evaluation are Healthy with null evaluation timestamps.

403.description: Authentication error or missing email sending read permission.

post.description: Send an email for the specified account using the structured builder. Provide the sender, recipients, subject, and at least one of text or html; attachments are optional.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the account.

400.description: Invalid request, generally because of the format/content of the email send request. No email will be sent when this happens.

403.description: Email sending is disabled, or the sending domain is not configured for email sending.

409.description: Email Sending setup is still in progress. Retry later; no email was sent.

429.description: Account/zone has surpassed the rate at which it can send email, please try again later. No email will be sent when this happens.

500.description: An unexpected error while processing the email send request. No email will be sent when this happens.

post.description: Send a raw RFC 5322 (MIME) email for the specified account. Provide the full MIME message plus the SMTP envelope (from and recipients).

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the account.

400.description: Invalid request, generally because of the format/content of the email send request. No email will be sent when this happens.

403.description: Email sending is disabled, or the sending domain is not configured for email sending.

409.description: Email Sending setup is still in progress. Retry later; no email was sent.

429.description: Account/zone has surpassed the rate at which it can send email, please try again later. No email will be sent when this happens.

500.description: An unexpected error while processing the email send request. No email will be sent when this happens.

get.description: Lists email suppressions for the specified account.

post.description: Creates a new email suppression for the specified account.

delete.description: Deletes an email suppression for the specified account.

get.description: Retrieves a single email suppression for the specified account.

Lists every active Email Sending suppression owned by the account: sending-domain suppressions first, then account-wide suppressions (including legacy rows with internal zone memberships). Each group is newest first.

schema.description: Maximum number of suppressions to return per page.
Opaque pagination cursor returned as `result_info.next_cursor`. It carries the filters that produced it.
A complete address is an exact match; a value ending in `@` matches that username across every domain. Prefix searches may return short intermediate pages while the bounded account scan advances.
Filter to suppressions with this reason.
Filter by scope: `account` returns only account-wide suppressions, `sending_domain` only sending-domain suppressions. Omit to list both, sending-domain suppressions first.

expires_at.description: When the suppression expires. Null for a permanent suppression.

note.description: Advisory note for this suppression, if any.

read_only.description: Whether clients may mutate this suppression. This is determined by the server and must not be inferred from `reason`.

reason.description: Why the address is suppressed: `manual`, `complaint`, `hard_bounce`, `soft_bounce`, or `policy`.

scope.description: Where the suppression applies: `account` for every sending domain of the account, or `sending_domain` for one envelope MAIL FROM domain.

type.description: Blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.
Blocks the recipient only for mail whose envelope MAIL FROM uses `value`.

value.description: The sending domain: the domain part of the envelope MAIL FROM, lowercase, without a trailing dot.

count.description: Number of suppressions in this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass it back as the `cursor` query parameter and continue until it is `null`. A bounded large-account scan may return a short intermediate page. Sending-domain suppressions are listed before account suppressions; each group is newest first.

per_page.description: Maximum number of suppressions requested per page.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, when one applies: `invalid_scope_value` (the sending domain is not valid), `scope_immutable` (scope cannot change after creation), or `scope_value_requires_type` (`scope_value` needs `scope_type=sending_domain`).

post.description: Creates a suppression for every sending domain of the account (default) or for one sending domain (`scope.type = sending_domain`). Creating an existing active suppression returns its identifier. If a mutable legacy zone-linked account row already exists, it is promoted without changing its identifier.

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp for the suppression. Omit or set to null for a permanent suppression that never expires.

note.description: Advisory note for this suppression. Not enforced or validated beyond length.

scope.description: Where the suppression applies. Omit for `{ "type": "account" }`, which blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.

type.description: Blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.
Blocks the recipient only for mail whose envelope MAIL FROM uses `value`.

value.description: The sending domain to suppress for: the domain part of the envelope MAIL FROM. It is lowercased and trailing dots are removed. Internationalized domains must use the ASCII (punycode) form. Ownership is not checked; a domain the account does not send from never matches.

scope.description: Where the suppression applies: `account` for every sending domain of the account, or `sending_domain` for one envelope MAIL FROM domain.

type.description: Blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.
Blocks the recipient only for mail whose envelope MAIL FROM uses `value`.

value.description: The sending domain: the domain part of the envelope MAIL FROM, lowercase, without a trailing dot.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, when one applies: `invalid_scope_value` (the sending domain is not valid), `scope_immutable` (scope cannot change after creation), or `scope_value_requires_type` (`scope_value` needs `scope_type=sending_domain`).

403.description: This suppression is read-only.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, when one applies: `invalid_scope_value` (the sending domain is not valid), `scope_immutable` (scope cannot change after creation), or `scope_value_requires_type` (`scope_value` needs `scope_type=sending_domain`).

Machine-readable error code, when one applies: `invalid_scope_value` (the sending domain is not valid), `scope_immutable` (scope cannot change after creation), or `scope_value_requires_type` (`scope_value` needs `scope_type=sending_domain`).

Machine-readable error code, when one applies: `invalid_scope_value` (the sending domain is not valid), `scope_immutable` (scope cannot change after creation), or `scope_value_requires_type` (`scope_value` needs `scope_type=sending_domain`).

post.summary: Bulk import account Email Sending suppressions
post.description: Imports up to 1,000 Email Sending suppressions in one request. Each item applies to every sending domain of the account (default) or to one sending domain.

items.description: Suppressions to import. Items with the same email address and scope are deduplicated before processing.

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp for the suppression. Omit or set to null for a permanent suppression that never expires.

note.description: Advisory note for this suppression. Not enforced or validated beyond length.

scope.description: Where the suppression applies. Omit for `{ "type": "account" }`, which blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.

If the zone lacks a DMARC TXT record of its own, the API resolves _dmarc.{zone} recursively and evaluates whatever that lookup returns. A CNAME at _dmarc.{zone} that points to a valid DMARC record is therefore healthy; the cname-on-dmarc-record value means the CNAME resolves to no DMARC record at all.

resolved.description: For a CNAME record, the TXT content(s) found by following the CNAME chain to its target. An empty array means the chain was resolved but nothing usable was found there; omitted/null means resolution was not attempted for this record (always the case for non-CNAME entries). A CNAME chain that terminates in more than one TXT value at the target yields multiple entries. Populated on entries in cname_dmarc_records, cname_spf_records, and cname_dkim_records.

type.description: Record type

email-auth_InspectError.description: An error encountered during SPF inspection

code.description:
Error code. Known values:
- `lookup_failed` — DNS TXT lookup failed
- `spf_not_found` — no SPF record found
- `invalid_spf` — record does not start with `v=spf1`
- `invalid_domain` — PSL validation failed
- `loop_detected` — include/redirect cycle detected
- `invalid_mechanism` — unrecognised or malformed mechanism
- `resource_limit_exceeded` — internal resource protection limits exceeded (recursion depth or query budget)
- `max_lookups` — RFC 7208 10-lookup limit exceeded

details.description:
Additional error-specific details (optional).
- For `invalid_domain` errors: the invalid domain string
- For `invalid_mechanism` errors: the invalid mechanism text (e.g., "invalidmech123")
- For `loop_detected` errors: the domain that caused the loop
- For other error types: not present

email-auth_ResolvedDmarcRecord.description: A DMARC TXT record that a recursive lookup of _dmarc.{zone} returned. Such a record usually lives in another zone outside this account's control, so this schema omits the DNS record ID. The API therefore treats such a record as read-only.

content.description: The TXT record value. The API joins all character-strings into a single string.

email-auth_SpfComponent.description:
A single SPF component (mechanism) in the inspection tree.

The `value` field includes the qualifier prefix (e.g., "-all", "~mx:example.com")
to match the raw SPF record syntax. The qualifier is also available separately
in the `result` field for programmatic access.

lookup_count.description:
Number of DNS lookups this component requires (per RFC 7208).
- MX, A, EXISTS, INCLUDE, REDIRECT, PTR: 1
- IP4, IP6, ALL: 0

nested.description:
Nested SPF tree for INCLUDE or REDIRECT mechanisms.
Only present for INCLUDE/REDIRECT components.

type.description: Component type (UPPERCASE)

value.description:
Component value with qualifier prefix.
For IP4/IP6, stores just the IP address (no "ip4:" or "ip6:" prefix).
Examples: "203.0.113.1", "203.0.113.0/24", "2001:db8::1/64", "-all", "~mx:example.com", "include:_spf.example.com"

errors.description:
All errors encountered during inspection, collected from the entire tree.
This includes errors from nested includes at any depth, providing a quick
overview of all issues without needing to traverse the nested structure.
Each error includes a `domain` field to identify where it occurred.
Empty array if no errors (omitted from JSON when empty).

total_lookups.description: Total number of DNS lookups performed across all includes

email_sending_subdomain_config_error.description: A DNS record, sending-configuration, or policy issue detected during preview, status, or fix.

code.description:
Error code identifying the type of issue. `dkim.conflict` is
reported whenever 2+ TXT records exist at the DKIM selector,
even if one matches the canonical Cloudflare content — multi-record
DKIM can permerror at recipient verification regardless of which
entry is correct. `domainkey.delegated` indicates that
`_domainkey.<subdomain>` has NS records in the Cloudflare zone,
creating a zone cut that shadows the DKIM TXT record we publish;
the customer must remove the NS delegation for DKIM to verify.
`dmarc.incompatible` indicates that a wildcard sending row no longer
satisfies its DMARC safety requirements, such as relaxed alignment,
a valid governing policy, and the organizational-domain constraint.
The customer must correct the zone or policy configuration manually;
DNS Fix cannot resolve this error.
`sending_subdomain.conflict` is reported by preview when an enabled
explicit or wildcard sending row would give some senders a different
signing identity.

conflicting_subdomain.description: The enabled sending-subdomain row that conflicts with the requested name.

multiple.description: Multiple conflicting DNS records found, for example more than one SPF or DMARC TXT record.
